title: The great leveller in reverse
text: A mother of two teenagers writes that social media makes us compare others' curated highlights with our own unfiltered lives. Quoting James Clear, 'Comparison is useful as a point and destructive as a loop.' Her answer: name the comparison, curate the feed, treat others' success as a mirror, and measure yourself against who you were yesterday.
use: For 'Social media is Triggering Fear of Missing Out amongst the youth' (2024), 'The process of self-discovery has now been technologically outsourced' (2021) and 'Social media is inherently a selfish medium' (2017).

title: From access to judgement
text: India has over a billion internet users, but only 18% of adults can file a cybercrime complaint online. As generative AI makes fakes cheap, 'the question is no longer how to access information, but how to judge what is reliable'. Children meet AI-shaped feeds before they can question them.
use: For 'A well-educated mind will always have more questions than answers' (2026) and 'Biased media is a real threat to Indian democracy' (2019).

title: AI and the end of 'safe' jobs
text: Microsoft offered exits to 60,000 staff, 27% of its workforce, as AI lets firms do more with fewer people; banks and tech giants shed staff in 2026 even as profits grew.
use: For 'Rise of Artificial Intelligence: the threat of jobless future or better job opportunities through reskilling and upskilling' and technology essays.
